mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a deflationary shock.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a supply-side shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings for industrial firms and drags S&P 500 returns lower over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous surge in commodity prices.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual tightening of monetary and price pressures, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL > 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a supply-chain normalization.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA by > 10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.8%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous spike in mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates a paradoxical labor market signal where headline employment growth coexists with deteriorating labor force participation, suggesting structural shifts that depress productivity and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises while UNRATE rises over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of rapid automation adoption.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 2% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based collapse in consumer demand, which reduces revenue expectations across sectors and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by > 2% month-over-month for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous surge in household savings rates.
